title: 6 white-gauze qipao studio dance clips cut into one 16.8s video: where to put the joins, what order avoids jumps?
summary: Fix the order first, then pick the cut points. The worst jump drops from 3.31x in the straight concat to 2.07x in the fine cut (1 = the footage's normal motion level): 31.0s of raw footage cut into a 16.75s final video with its original audio.

items.label: Fine Cut Final video 16.75s · Watch it start to finish and keep your eye on the 5 joins for any visible jump · ★ recommended
Fine Cut Control: straight concat in original order, 31.0s · See where each boundary jumps — the worst is 3.31x, while the fine cut at the same spots is only 2.07x
Fine Cut Pre-cut check · 5 side-by-side pairs of "last frame of A | first frame of B", checked group by group for whether the motion connects
Fine Cut Full-video spot check · 2fps × 36 contact-sheet frames, scanned in cell order for breaks in rhythm or pose
Fine Cut Design frame · Studio front full-body shot, shared as the first frame by 4 clips; compare against the final video to check the character hasn't drifted
Fine Cut Design frame · Back view in a light breeze, shared as the first frame by the other 2 clips; covers the two slow-motion shots at the end

stats: One 16.75s final video with its original audio, about half of the 31.0s of raw footage: 544×960 portrait · 24fps constant frame rate (CFR) · SAR 1:1 · H.264 CRF16 slow · AAC 32kHz · 7.48MB
6 clips (takes) of one dance from the same prompt groups, 5.17s each, three sizes at 0.4/0.5/0.98MP → 480×864 / 544×960 / 768×1344, plus 2 first-frame design images
How the cut points were picked

Scale frames down to 40×52 grayscale, diff adjacent frames at 12fps, and brute-force all 30 ordered pairs (last 2.5s of A × first 2.5s of B); the closest frame lands right in the middle of the dissolve
How the six clips are ordered
00273→00276→00274→00278→00277→00275: big moves up front, slow shots at the end, and the two near-identical clips pulled apart

All 5 joins use dissolves: 0.22s between dance clips; 0.35s at joins that cross background audio tracks (between J-pop music and ambient sound); the final 0.55s fades picture and sound to white together
Straight concat ▮▮▮▮▮ 2.73~3.31x → fine cut ▮▮▮ 1.63~2.07x (1 = the footage's normal motion level); the last cut at 0.89x is barely visible
Trimming the 6 clips, white padding, 5 picture+audio dissolves (xfade/acrossfade), and the white fade-out all go into one filter chain (filter_complex) - done in a single encode, no second pass
findings: Order is worth more than cut points: with the exact same scan results, only the order of the six clips changes, and the worst join drops from 3.11x to 2.42x - the original order wedged a near-static slow shot between big-move dance clips, and that cut jumped the hardest

Frame diffing has a floor: scan every pairing of the 6 clips and the best pair still sits at 1.64x (big dance moves, and a pure-white background gives no edge reference), so a seamless hard cut is off the table; the leftover 1.6~2.4x gap is smoothed by the 0.22s dissolves

Cutting the parts nobody watches saves the most runtime: every clip starts on an idle stance and ends on a settle (motion under 0.6x of normal); trimming them takes 31.0s down to 16.75s, and the perceived density nearly doubles

The two clip groups carry different background-audio prompts (J-pop / soft-breeze ambience), so after reordering the video naturally runs "music section → ambient sound close"; joins that cross background tracks use the longer 0.35s dissolve so picture and sound change together
With a pure-white studio background you must pad with white: black bars read as smudges on a white frame - the pad color follows the scene, it is not the default black
Frame diffs cannot read motion meaning: two frames spinning in opposite directions can still score close, so eyeball the "last frame | first frame" pairs before any cut
